subject: fla IS used in training; GPU memory clean after OOM probes
body:
Re: throughput results (282685a50e23a1d7).

1. CUDA memory after your two OOM probes: clean. nvidia-smi shows 15 MiB used, 0 % utilisation, no compute processes. Both jobs (j-20261008-112600-5b3a8b pid 810225, j-20261008-112603-bbbc11 pid 852156) are recorded as failed with 'exit code 1', and neither pid is still alive. No jobs are queued or running.

2. Why there was no speedup versus yesterday: your baseline already had the fast path. flash-linear-attention/fla-core 0.5.2 were installed at 2026-10-07 17:10:38Z and causal-conv1d 1.7.0 at 17:39:05Z. Your first bridge runs started at 22:23Z, five hours later. There is no no-fla baseline from the bridge. The only one is my direct toy run from before the install: 0.285 s/example without causal-conv1d versus 0.241 s/example with it.

3. Training does use the fla kernels. I ran a torch.profiler pass on a 2048-token forward+backward of Qwen3.5-0.8B-Base (bf16 weights, train mode, gradient checkpointing; same venv and HF_HOME as the bridge jobs). Total CUDA self time was 803 ms, and the run took 0.768 s.
   - fla Triton kernels, forward and backward: chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_kernel_h_blockdim64 (12.9 ms, x54), chunk_bwd_kernel_dqkwg (9.2), chunk_gated_delta_rule_bwd_kernel_dhu_blockdim64 (8.1), chunk_fwd_kernel_o (7.6), prepare_wy_repr_bwd_kernel (6.7), l2norm fwd/bwd (7.9), chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_kkt_solve_kernel (3.0).
   - causal-conv1d CUDA kernels: causal_conv1d_channellast_fwd/bwd_kernel (7.1 + 6.0 ms).
   - Together the gated-delta and conv kernels are about 72 ms, roughly 9 % of GPU time. Flash-attention kernels for the full-attention layers add about 26 ms.
   - The rest is bf16 GEMMs: the top 4 kernels are about 470 ms, roughly 58 %, plus about 50 ms of dtype-copy kernels.
   So the fast path is active but small. The model is GEMM-bound, which matches your ~1.0-1.3K tok/s plateau. The reference PyTorch fallback mostly hurt the delta-rule part, which is now about 9 % of time.

4. Possible cheap speedup, untested on Kev: the default --weights_dtype fp32 + --dtype bf16 autocast re-casts the frozen backbone every forward pass, which is the dtype-copy kernels above. --weights_dtype bf16 halves backbone memory and removes those casts. It may also free enough VRAM for batch>1 at 300-2K tokens. Worth one A/B through the bridge, with a quality check, since the checkpoint records weights_dtype.

Services are up: bridge, tunnel, chat watcher, nosleep. Standing by for the wave-1 kev.train jobs.
